rules.title: Broker fee paid only by the party who hired the broker
rules.requirement: In Massachusetts, a rental broker's fee may be charged only to the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired and contracted with the broker. If the landlord hired the broker, you as a tenant cannot be made to pay that fee.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party who engaged the broker

coverage.summary: All residential rental transactions in Massachusetts involving a licensed real estate broker or salesperson finding dwelling accommodations.

rules.citation: M.G.L. c. 112 § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43)
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Only licensed brokers may charge fees for finding rental housing
rules.requirement: Only a licensed real estate broker or salesperson may charge a fee for finding an apartment for a prospective tenant. Do not pay a finder's fee to an unlicensed person.

coverage.summary: All residential rental housing in Massachusetts where a person charges a fee for finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants.

rules.quoted_span: No person shall engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless such person is a licensed broker or salesman as defined in section eighty-seven PP of chapter one hundred and twelve.

notes: Page shows both the pre-August 1, 2025 text and the text as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43 effective August 1, 2025. The broker-fee payment rule comes from the amended text, which is in force as of 2026-10-01. The licensing requirement appears in both versions; the document gives no original effective date for it.
